newsitem.title: USA: FOB Gulf Grain - Corn steady to firmer, soy flat.
newsitem.headline: FOB Gulf Grain - Corn steady to firmer, soy flat.

text.p: FOB Gulf corn basis values were steady to one cent a bushel firmer in the nearby positions on Monday while soybeans and wheat were flat.
The nearby corn positions were up due to thin supplies in the export pipeline, one dealer said. "Farmers are just waiting" for higher prices, the dealer added.
Also, soybeans were being harvested in the U.S. Midwest but nobody has seen any real significant movement in that commodity as well, the dealer said.

In export news, South Korea's Cheiljedang Corp bought 35,000 tonnes of U.S. No 2 soybean at basis over November futures on CBOT. The company bought the soybeans from Marubeni Corp for shipment in early November from the U.S. Gulf. Arrival was set for the port city of Inchon.

Taiwan's Hui Shung Group will tender on Tuesday for a combined shipment of 38,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn for December 5-20, U.S. Gulf and/or December 21-January 4, PNW.
And China late last week bought between 120,000-150,000 tonnes of soymeal for November and December delivery from the United States, South America and India, Hong Kong-based traders said on Monday.
